sections.h2: Finishes with texture, depth, and character
body: Flat paint is a single even color. Decorative finishes are layered, hand-worked, and change as the light moves across them. They suit feature walls, entries, powder rooms, dining rooms, fireplace surrounds, and exteriors where you want an aged or mineral look rather than a uniform film.

Because these finishes depend on the hand that applies them, the process is slower and more deliberate than standard interior painting. That is the point. Every wall ends up slightly different, and that variation is what makes it look crafted rather than manufactured.

sections.h2: Limewash on Florida brick and block
body: Limewash has become a favorite for brick and painted block homes around Gainesville and Ocala, and it earns that. It is a mineral finish that soaks into the masonry instead of forming a film on top, so it breathes freely, does not trap moisture, and wears down softly over years instead of peeling. Many owners like that slightly weathered, chalky look on ranch homes and fireplace walls.

It is also unforgiving. Every stop and start shows, so limewash is applied by brush in continuous passes, wall to wall, and the masonry is dampened first so it absorbs evenly. The amount of brick showing through can be controlled during application and adjusted afterward by washing back. On masonry with past paint, the old coating may need to be removed first, which we check on the walkthrough. If your goal is solid color rather than a washed look, our masonry painting service is the better fit.

Venetian plaster is built in thin, troweled layers that are burnished to anything from a soft stone look to a polished sheen with real depth. It is durable, works well in powder rooms, entries, and accent walls, and can be sealed with a protective wax or topcoat in damp areas. Because the walls must be very flat, drywall is repaired and skimmed first; our drywall repair crew handles that prep.

Metallic and pearlescent finishes reflect light differently through the day and are popular on ceilings, niches, and behind beds or bars. Glazes add soft color variation over a base coat. All of these rely on careful base preparation so the decorative layer has a smooth, sound surface to sit on.

Plaster and glaze work also lets you reach a look that would otherwise mean costly materials. A troweled lime plaster can read like honed stone on a fireplace surround, and a layered glaze can make a plain drywall niche feel aged. When an older home already has a hand-applied finish that was damaged by a repair, we can often match it rather than painting the whole room flat, using test patches until the color, texture, and sheen line up.

sections.h2: Sample boards before anything goes on the wall
body: With decorative work, the sample process matters more than the calendar. Absorbency of the surface, pressure of the trowel or brush, and the light in your room all change the result. We make sample boards on site, using your actual color choices, and leave them with you for a day or two so you can see them morning, noon, and night.

If you are unsure where to start on colors, our color consultation service can help narrow options for plaster tones, limewash shades, and the wall colors around a feature finish. For homes with historic character, our post on historic paint colors in Gainesville offers ideas that suit older architecture.

Limewash exteriors are expected to soften with weather and can be refreshed with another coat years later without stripping. Venetian plaster is hard and long lasting; small dings can usually be filled and re-burnished. Metallic finishes should be cleaned gently with a soft cloth rather than scrubbed. We leave labelled materials and care notes so future touch-ups match.
Decorative finishes are part of our specialty services and are quoted in writing like everything else: surfaces included, the finish and product, number of layers, and the schedule.

Most decorative finishes are best applied in conditioned interiors or, for limewash on exteriors, during the drier months from October through May, when humidity is lower and the mineral finish cures evenly. We schedule around that so your result looks the way the sample board did.

faqs.q: Is limewash good for Florida homes?
faqs.a: Yes, on suitable masonry. It is breathable and wears gradually instead of peeling. Surfaces with existing paint may need it removed first, and we check that before quoting.

faqs.q: Can I see the finish before you do the whole wall?
faqs.a: Always. We make sample boards on site with your colors and leave them with you before any wall is started.

faqs.q: Can Venetian plaster go in a bathroom?
faqs.a: It can in powder rooms and many baths when sealed appropriately. Direct shower spray is a different situation, and we will advise on the right product.

faqs.q: How long does a decorative finish take?
faqs.a: It depends on the finish and area. Plaster and layered glazes need dry time between layers, so they take longer than standard paint. The schedule is on your estimate.
